recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is recommended for FHIR-19824 unless the work group separately chooses to do editorial cleanup of the HTTP narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-19824 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for FHIR-core HTTP Batch/Transaction Response wording. It asked to clarify that response entries include the HTTP status code and, where applicable, Location and ETag header values, rather than implying Location or ETag are always required.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit a1efcc18b1f95aac0fa4f5f6246e69e9b59469b6, which updated source/http.html to add the "where applicable" clarification for Location and ETag and to mark up/capitalize those header names. Current source/http.html still contains that wording.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2019-07-01 record agreement to reword GF 19824 to clarify ETag and Location header requirements with a 6-0-0 Persuasive vote. The adjacent Bundle definitions remain consistent: Bundle.entry.response.location is optional and populated if an operation returns a location, while Bundle.entry.response.etag is optional and relevant when processing produced a versioned resource. Community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The important conformance clarification from the Jira resolution is already in source/http.html. The retained "which are used for identifying and versioning" clause is explanatory and does not conflict with the clarified where-applicable requirement, so removing it would be editorial cleanup rather than a necessary current-spec correction.
